newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher after storage data.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher after storage data.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open higher Thursday after paltry storage injection data sent August soaring to a new contract high on ACCESS, sources said.
September over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.48 to $2.51 after settling to the upside Wednesday at $2.351 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, September set a new contract high of $2.505 before last trading at $2.475, up 12.4 cents.
Early cash prices at Henry Hub were talked more than 10 cents higher at $2.50-2.52. At the Chicago city-gate, prices were talked around $2.60.
Helping to fuel the rally on ACCESS was news from American Gas Association that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 55 bcf, well below average estimates of 70-75 bcf.

Overall inventories were 133 bcf, or 7.5 percent, above last year's record lows. Eastern inventories increased by 50 bcf and remained 28 bcf, or three percent, over last year. Consuming region west storage, which gained seven bcf last week, continued to lag 1996 levels by about one percent. Stocks in the producing region, which fell two bcf for the week, were still 28 percent above last year.
Chart traders pegged September resistance at the new contract high of $2.505 and then near $2.55 along the uptrend line. Support was seen at $2.34-2.345, and then at $2.30 and $2.20.
In Wednesday's cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed five cents to the mid-$2.30s. Midcon pipes were up a few cents to near $2.30, while New York city gate prices held in the low-$2.50s.
Temperatures are moderating throughout most of the U.S. and are expected to reach above-normal levels by the weekend in parts of the East, Midwest and Texas, according to Weather Services Corp.
